checks.description: activation: TrainUnitsMode's screen-before-recovery exemption is now bounded by the screen attrition tally it already keeps. Last fight the Vehicle queue issued 8 orders in 1332s and 5 were bggy (218s, 244s, 427s, 458s, 477s), every one carrying 'first light screen before harvester recovery' - the literal that says recovery had chosen harv and the exemption overruled it. A 300-credit vehicle living a mean of 50.4s is never standing, so the exemption was permanently on. This id is emitted only when the tally is what changed the answer and a harvester came out.

activation: the mid-game reservation recorded economy.bank-replaces-harvester at none of last fight's 267 assessments. Its floor of four refineries was not met until 455s and BaseUnderAttack read true at every assessment from 405s onward, so the rule was unreachable by construction. The floor now reads OpeningBankTuning.RefineryFloor so the handover is exact, and the release is proportionate (enemy value at the base above own army value there) rather than any sighting at all.

outcome: the direct measure. Six harvesters existed all match (three of them refinery free actors), the fleet peaked at five against the eight docking places four refineries provide, and the last harvester ordered before the collapse was at 344s - 940 seconds before the next one. Note units.count(type=harv) counts BOTH sides (14 last fight against this side's 6), which is why this reads the summary ledger instead.

outcome: 862 of 1332 seconds had no live harvester and lifetime earnings froze at 15,435 credits from 480s. Every credit after that came from nowhere, so the side produced nothing at all for its last 840 seconds. If the fleet is replaced while it is being hunted, this is where it shows.

outcome: 11.588 credits a second against a reference of 50 and a prior median of 35.573, the worst earning rate in the trend window. While harvesters lived the side earned roughly 40 a second, so this is a fleet-size problem rather than a harvesting problem: 15,435 credits earned in a match the opponent finished with an army worth 75,150.

invariant: a reservation that strangles the barracks is the failure mode both of these changes sit one step away from. Only the last 1,100 credits are defended, the reservation stands down for sixty seconds whenever it has not grown the fleet, and it releases outright when the enemy at the base outvalues the army standing in it. Spend was 17.218 a second last match against a prior median of 42.203; holding cash nothing spends would push it lower still.

invariant: the same risk measured on the queue rather than the rate. The Infantry queue issued 33 orders last match and its rungs are capped at four bodies while income is short, not silenced. A reservation that reached the barracks would show as this collapsing.

outcome: fitness 0.268 against a prior median of 0.656, with economicRate 0.232, valueExchange 0.203 and armyValueIntegral 0.065 all near their floors. All three are paid for by income, so a working fleet should move the total rather than one component.
